title: Uniform two-open locality of perfect-arrow coherent coefficient factorization
statement:
Let $D$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $D\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, and let $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ be separated and of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions]. For every quasi-compact open subscheme $W\subseteq Y$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], put $\mathcal B_W=\mathcal O_W\otimes_D R_A$ and use $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal B_W)$, the forgetful functor $U_W$, perfection, $\widehat K$, and the coefficient constructions of [def-sfb-dg-coefficient-realization] on $W$. For a commutative $D$-algebra $E$ with a specified map $E\to A$, put $W_E=W\times_D\operatorname{Spec}E$ and let $\pi_{W,E}:W_A\to W_E$ be the projection [def-pc-fibre-product]; write $\Phi^W_E$ and $\nu^W_E$ for those coefficient constructions.

Define $\mathscr P(W)$ as the following uniform assertion. For every perfect $H\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal B_W)$, every $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{W_A})$ [def-pc-derived-category], every $m\in\mathbf Z$, and every morphism $u:H\to\widehat K$ such that $H^i(U_Wu)$ is surjective as a morphism of sheaves for every $i\ge m$, there exist a commutative finite type $D$-algebra $E$ with $D\to E\to A$, an object $G\in D(\mathcal O_{W_E})$ with bounded coherent cohomology [pqf-def-coherent], an ordinary scheme-derived morphism $\gamma:G\to R\pi_{W,E*}K$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image], and a morphism $\sigma:H\to\Phi^W_E(G)$ in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal B_W)$ such that $\nu^W_E(\gamma)\circ\sigma=u$ and $H^i(U_W\sigma)$ is surjective for every $i\ge m$.

Let $O,V$ be quasi-compact open subschemes of $Y$, with $V$ affine [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $O\cap V$ quasi-compact. If $\mathscr P(O)$, $\mathscr P(V)$ and $\mathscr P(O\cap V)$ hold, then $\mathscr P(O\cup V)$ holds. Each premise quantifies over all the indicated sources, targets, cutoffs and cohomologically surjective arrows on its own open, including ones not obtained by restricting any fixed global data. The coefficient algebras and witnesses may depend on these inputs. No compatibility between chosen witnesses, flatness of coefficient maps, relative pseudo-coherence of $K$, or injectivity of $H^i(U_Wu)$ is assumed.

source.place: Agent-formulated UNIFORM conditional two-open locality subproblem below the unnumbered Kiehl assertion following Tag 0CSD (lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general). The predicate covers all perfect sources, ordinary targets and arrows surjective on cohomology above every cutoff. This locality assertion is not stated there. WANTED: Kiehl (1972), Ein Descente-Lemma und Grothendiecks Projektionssatz fuer nichtnoethersche Schemata, Math. Ann. 198, pp.287--316, finite coherent coefficient-model descent. Assembly follows coherent.tex Tag 08DR (lemma-induction-principle); ordinary gluing in cohomology.tex Tag 08DG (lemma-glue) alone does not supply this assertion.

proof.text: Set $W=O\cup V$. It is quasi-compact since a finite union of quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact. Fix arbitrary $H,K,m,u$ as quantified in $\mathscr P(W)$. If $W$ is empty take $E=D$, $G=0$, $\gamma=0$, and $\sigma=0$; every sheaf in question is zero. In the remaining steps assume $W$ is nonempty. The three uniform local premises will be retained for every degree of the induction; they are not replaced by a choice of witnesses for restrictions of this fixed arrow.

source.place: Agent finite downward induction for the uniform locality subproblem beneath the unnumbered Kiehl assertion after Tag 0CSD (lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general). Perfect descent analogy: Tag 09RF (lemma-descend-perfect); ordinary gluing input only: cohomology.tex Tag 08DG (lemma-glue).

proof.text: Apply perfect sheaf dg descent on this quasi-compact open $W$. Obtain $E$ finite type over $D$, a perfect $H_E$ over $\mathcal C_E=\mathcal O_W\otimes_D R_E$, and $\alpha:\mathcal B_W\otimes_{\mathcal C_E}^{\mathbf L}H_E\simeq H$. Scalar adjunction transposes $u\alpha$ to $a:H_E\to\operatorname{Res}_{\mathcal C_E}\widehat K$. The target has its action through $\mathcal T_E=\mathcal O_W\otimes_D E=p_{E*}\mathcal O_{W_E}$, since $\widehat K$ carries the given $A$-action and $D\to E\to A$ is a commuting base triangle. Adjunction along the augmentation $\mathcal C_E\to\mathcal T_E$ therefore transposes $a$ to $c:F\to\operatorname{Res}_{\mathcal T_E}\widehat K$, where $F=\mathcal T_E\otimes_{\mathcal C_E}^{\mathbf L}H_E$. Both adjunctions use left modules, through the opposite-algebra clause of the cited adjunction theorem.

source.place: Agent finite downward induction for the uniform locality subproblem beneath the unnumbered Kiehl assertion after Tag 0CSD (lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general). Perfect descent analogy: Tag 09RF (lemma-descend-perfect); ordinary gluing input only: cohomology.tex Tag 08DG (lemma-glue).

proof.text: The map $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ is affine by the affine-schemes lemma, so its base change $p_E:W_E\to W$ is affine by permanence. On each affine open of $W$, the affine dg comparison identifies $F$ with an ordinary perfect complex on its $E$-base change. Thus $F$ has quasi-coherent $\mathcal T_E$-cohomology. The derived affine-morphism equivalence for $p_E:W_E\to W$ gives an ordinary object $G$ with $Rp_{E*}G\simeq F$. The projection $\pi_{W,E}:W_A\to W_E$ is the base change of the affine morphism $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}E$, hence affine by the same two lemmas, so the affine derived-cohomology lemma gives $R\pi_{W,E*}K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{W_E})$ and $Rp_{E*}R\pi_{W,E*}K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal T_E)$; full faithfulness of the equivalence therefore applies to this target. It carries $c$ to an ordinary morphism $\gamma:G\to R\pi_{W,E*}K$, using the coefficient-linear composition identification in the definition of $\widehat K$ and $\nu_E$. Local perfectness of $G$ follows from the same affine comparison. To check bounded coherence, cover $W$ by finitely many affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}S_j$. Each $S_j$ is finite type over $D$ by the affine-pairs criterion for $Y/D$. Their $E$-base changes have rings $S_j\otimes_D E$, finite type over $D$ by the two finite generating lists. They are Noetherian. These finitely many affines cover $W_E$, making it Noetherian. The perfect-cohomology theorem now makes $G$ bounded coherent.

source.place: Agent finite downward induction for the uniform locality subproblem beneath the unnumbered Kiehl assertion after Tag 0CSD (lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general). Perfect descent analogy: Tag 09RF (lemma-descend-perfect); ordinary gluing input only: cohomology.tex Tag 08DG (lemma-glue).

proof.text: Let $\eta:H_E\to\operatorname{Res}_{\mathcal C_E}F$ be the augmentation adjunction unit. Define $s:H\to\Phi^W_E(G)$ as $\alpha^{-1}$ followed by derived extension of $\eta$ to $\mathcal B_W$. The adjunction equation $\operatorname{Res}(c)\eta=a$, followed by the other adjunction's action counit, gives $\nu^W_E(\gamma)s=u$. This is the action counit specified in the coefficient definition, not a map selected by cohomology. Choose $b_G$ with $H^i(G)=0$ for $i>b_G$. On the same finite affine cover the comparison represents $Rp_{E*}G$ by ordinary module complexes zero above $b_G$. The relative bar model for $R_E\to R_A$ has terms $R_A\otimes_D R_E^{\otimes_D n}\otimes_D M[n]$. Both coefficient algebras are nonpositive, and the shift $[n]$ lowers degrees by $n\ge0$, so these terms are zero above $b_G$. Thus $H^i(U_W\Phi^W_E(G))=0$ for $i>b_G$, as can be checked on this cover. Put $b=\max(m,b_G)$. The supplied $s$ is surjective in degrees $i>b$, because its target is zero there.

source.place: Agent finite downward induction for the uniform locality subproblem beneath the unnumbered Kiehl assertion after Tag 0CSD (lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general). Perfect descent analogy: Tag 09RF (lemma-descend-perfect); ordinary gluing input only: cohomology.tex Tag 08DG (lemma-glue).

proof.text: Starting with the supplied global factorization of step 4, descend through $r=b,b-1,\ldots,m$. At the start of a stage the invariant is a finite type $D$-algebra $E$ mapping to $A$, a bounded-coherent $G$, an ordinary $\gamma$, and $s$ with $\nu^W_E(\gamma)s=u$ and $H^i(U_Ws)$ surjective for $i>r$. The three local uniform assertions remain those for the original $D\to A$ and the original opens. Since $r\ge m$, the hypothesis on $u$ gives surjectivity of $H^i(U_Wu)$ for every $i\ge r$. These are precisely the premises of the binary single-degree quotient lemma. It produces $E',G',\gamma',s'$ with the same composite $u$, ordinary $\gamma'$, bounded coherence, and surjectivity for all $i\ge r$. The map $E\to E'\to A$ extends the supplied coefficient map. Appending the finitely many generators of $E'/E$ to those of $E/D$ proves that $E'/D$ is finite type. Hence its output is the invariant for the next integer $r-1$. No new local predicate over $E$ is being assumed.

source.place: Agent finite downward induction for the uniform locality subproblem beneath the unnumbered Kiehl assertion after Tag 0CSD (lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general). Perfect descent analogy: Tag 09RF (lemma-descend-perfect); ordinary gluing input only: cohomology.tex Tag 08DG (lemma-glue).

proof.text: After $b-m+1$ stages, the final $E,G,\gamma,s$ have $\nu^W_E(\gamma)s=u$ and $H^i(U_Ws)$ surjective for every $i\ge m$. These are exactly the witnesses required for the fixed arbitrary $H,K,m,u$. Universal generalization gives $\mathscr P(W)$ and hence the claimed implication. The finite iteration is meaningful for every integer $m$, including negative cutoffs; there is no infinite descent.
